time.desc: A diplomat who has long been a mediator publicly stated that the two countries are close to reaching an indirect agreement on nuclear issues and sanctions.

The confrontation between the two countries turned from negotiations to open war: one side and its allies launched large-scale air strikes against the other side and claimed to carry out "decapitation" strikes.
For the first time since the war started, one side's military has publicly acknowledged the casualties and reported that the casualties came from the other side's drone counterattack.
The rival military launched a new missile offensive and fired missiles at an opponent's warship, while denying that it had closed the key strait.
The attacked side officially confirmed the emergence of a new supreme leader during the war to replace the former supreme leader who was killed in the attack on the first day of the war.

For the first time, security figures from allies of the party that launched the air strikes admitted that the air strikes lacked a feasible plan for regime change and that the rival regime continued to exist after the attack on the leader.

The warring parties carried out air strikes on the air defense and naval facilities of the opponent's largest crude oil export hub. Multiple explosions were heard on the island, raising the risk of energy exports.

When the leader of one country was interviewed, he questioned the life and death of his opponent's new supreme leader and said that the opponent's agreement terms were not good enough. The opponent issued an open letter stating that he was willing to negotiate with mutual respect but would not give in.

A senior financial official from one side made a policy statement regarding shipping in the key strait: there is no objection to the passage of ships from some countries and the follow-up energy measures will be linked to the length of the war.
One of the opponent's highest-ranking officials (former speaker/secretary of an agency) was killed in an allied airstrike, becoming the highest-ranking official killed since the war began.

The coalition forces participating in the war launched a new round of air strikes on the opponent's giant natural gas fields at sea. Shipping in the key strait was effectively paralyzed, and international oil and gas prices rose in response.

The leader of one side issued a time-limited ultimatum to the other side, demanding the resumption of commercial shipping in key straits and threatening to attack the other side's power and other energy facilities.

The opponent's military statement warned that if the opponent carried out an attack on its energy facilities, it would completely close the key strait, and the opponent threatened "unprecedented bombing" and the imposition of tariffs.
After the ultimatum, it was announced that the two sides had started dialogue and promised to suspend attacks on the other party's energy facilities for a few days to allow a window for negotiation.
One party formally submits a ceasefire/end-of-conflict plan containing multiple provisions to the other party to promote negotiations.
The other party completed a formal response to the multi-term ceasefire plan, bringing the negotiation to a new stage.
The two major powers outside the region jointly proposed another multi-point plan for a ceasefire and the restoration of normal traffic in the strait to promote an end to the war.
Leader A publicly called on all countries to go to Strait A to seize oil on their own, saying that Country X had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply.

The leader of one side delivered a national address, saying that he would carry out harsher attacks on his opponents in the coming weeks and also declared his intention to end the conflict as soon as possible.
